recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow correction to active Procedure narrative; no further core source work is needed for FHIR-7123 unless the work group wants a broader editorial refresh of Procedure notes.
issue_request: FHIR-7123 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1 Procedure. It asked to clarify the difference between Procedure.category and the then-named Procedure.type by renaming type/name on Procedure and ProcedureRequest, adding examples for category versus the specific procedure, and adding notes that related properties can sometimes be inferred from the procedure name/code.
initial_application: Commit 77c0aa01f08d8517bcba177c89b296095491221d explicitly cited #6129 and #7123 and renamed Procedure.type to Procedure.code, updated examples and profiles, and changed the Procedure binding from ProcedureType to ProcedureCode. Current Procedure.category and Procedure.code definitions already carry the requested high-level/specific-procedure distinction and examples.
additional_context: FHIR-6129 was later Published/Persuasive and changed the intermediate Procedure.name direction to Procedure.code for Procedure and ProcedureRequest. ProcedureRequest is no longer in the current build and its successor ServiceRequest has consistent category/code definitions. Procedure remains active in source/fhir.ini. Community searches found no relevant conflicting Zulip or Confluence discussion.
reconciliation: Changed source/procedure/procedure-notes.xml so the nonsensical-combination example says code=amputation instead of name=amputation. This removes the only discovered current-source drift from the FHIR-7123/FHIR-6129 application trail while preserving the original warning about inconsistent procedure code, body site, and inferred details.
source_changes: source/procedure/procedure-notes.xml: changed the obsolete example "name=amputation, bodySite=heart" to "code=amputation, bodySite=heart".
